bug_semantics: CRuby Nokogiri::XML::Node#initialize_copy_with_args is a protected copy helper behind Node#dup and #clone. It unwraps its source argument with Noko_Node_Get_Struct, which is a DATA_PTR cast to xmlNodePtr and performs no Ruby type check. Namespace is not a Node subclass and wraps xmlNs, which is smaller than xmlNode. If application code send-calls the helper with a non-Node (the vendor test is Node.allocate.send(:initialize_copy_with_args, namespace, 1, doc)), the C code treats an xmlNs as an xmlNode; noko_xml_document_pin_node then reads node->doc past the xmlNs object, a heap out-of-bounds read that crashes the process (CWE-843). Public #dup/#clone pass self, which is a Node, so normal API use and untrusted document input cannot trigger it. Only CRuby is affected; JRuby uses asXmlNode. Nokogiri 1.19.4 raises TypeError via rb_obj_is_kind_of before the unwrap.
flaw_origin: The argument-unwrap sink was first written in 1e7d38affc10917f12372fab97a505e6dbb8368b (PR #3117, 2024-01-31, Mike Dalessio) when CRuby Node#dup was replaced with Ruby Object#dup/#clone plus a new protected C helper so #clone would copy the singleton class (issue #316). That commit first defined rb_xml_node_initialize_copy_with_args, registered it as initialize_copy_with_args, and did Noko_Node_Get_Struct(rb_other, xmlNode, c_other) with no kind_of check, while the same change's JRuby path used asXmlNode. The immediate parent still implemented public Node#dup as duplicate_node, which unwrapped the receiver (self), not a caller-supplied source. Enabling Node.allocate in the same commit made the later PoC pattern possible but is not the type-confusion itself. Later c72503aad11821ad70d97a809087db02b21b9571 only appended node-cache/decorate after the same unchecked unwrap.
